messages:
Dmitri: Started a GPTQ sweep this morning across Llama-2-13b, Mistral-7b-v0, and Qwen-7b to compare GPTQ vs AWQ profiles. Posting quick heatmap and notes here.
Alice: Nice — did you include per-seq-len latency and KV cache behavior?
Dmitri: Yes. Short summary: AWQ gives smaller size on Mistral but we see ~6-12% accuracy delta on Llama in some prompt categories. KV cache thrashing observed on Qwen with our current converter.
Ben: Can you drop the failure cases? Which evals show regresses?
Dmitri: Mostly multi-turn commonsense and long-context code-cot. Example delta (accuracy @ top-1):
```
Llama-2-13b: FP32 87.1, GPTQ 86.5 (-0.6), AWQ 79.8 (-7.3)
Mistral-7b: FP32 84.4, GPTQ 84.0 (-0.4), AWQ 83.7 (-0.7)
Qwen-7b: FP32 85.9, GPTQ 85.3 (-0.6), AWQ 74.2 (-11.7)
```
Numbers are from the heldout 'prod-evals/v2' prompt set, sampling greedy for parity.
Carla: That's a big AWQ drop on Qwen. Could be quantization alignment or tokenizer mismatch in converter. Any log errors?
Dmitri: Converter logs show repeated KV dimension reorder warnings for Qwen at conversion time: `warn: kv_cache_permute mismatch` — found lines in conversion script where dim ordering assumed 2-nd axis. I pushed the minimal repro to s3:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-temp/qwen-kv-repro.tar.gz ./
python tools/convert_awq.py --model qwen-7b --verify-kv
```
Elaine: Repro looks solid. I also saw throughput regressions with AWQ on our 4090 fleet: latency up 8-15% for short seqs (<=128). For long seqs AWQ sometimes wins due to memory fit.
Ben: For Llama 13b the AWQ size win could matter for Dedicated, but if quality loss >1% it's worrying for Product teams.
Carla: Agreed. We should run focused per-task evals (summarization, code, multi-turn QA) with deterministic seeds + token-level diffs to classify regresses vs random noise.
Dmitri: Plan proposed: 1) Narrow AWQ params: block size 128/64 sweep, symmetric vs asymmetric; 2) Run per-task evals and token-diff collector; 3) Add KV-permute unit test to converter and CI gate; 4) For deployment, offer AWQ as "cost-tiered" variant behind opt-in feature flag.
Alice: Sounds good. For 1) do you have current command lines so others can reproduce?
Dmitri: Yep:
```
# example conversion
python tools/convert_gptq.py \
  --model-name-or-path llm/llama-2-13b \
  --bits 4 --group-size 128 --use-awq False \
  --out-dir /tmp/conv_llama13b_gptq

python tools/convert_awq.py \
  --src qwen/qwen-7b \
  --block-size 64 --symmetry asymmetric --out /tmp/conv_qwen_awq
```
Ben: Can we add a micro-benchmark for prefix cache reuse? I want numbers for cache-hit vs miss scenarios.
Elaine: I'll draft a micro-benchmark harness that runs repeating prefixes at different batch sizes and seq lengths; will post results by EOD.
quant-bot: conversion job 1938765900 finished: qwen-awq-block64 (succeeded), llm-mistral-gptq (succeeded), llm-llama13b-gptq (succeeded). Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/gptq-sweep/1938765900/
Carla: Great. Next immediate action items:
- Dmitri: add KV-permute unit test + open PR.
- Elaine: micro-benchmark harness + initial perf table.
- Ben: curate the per-task prompt subsets for deterministic runs.
- Alice: write short note for Product about opt-in AWQ risk profile.
Dmitri: I'll start the PR and tag reviewers. One more note: for deployment profiles, recommend default = GPTQ for now, AWQ only on Mistral-7b family and as opt-in for Qwen after converter fix and re-eval.
Alice: Thanks — keeping Product looped is key. Also let's capture cost-per-token delta in console for these variants so customers can opt based on clear tradeoffs.
Ben: Agreed. If AWQ gives >20% cost saving with <0.5% quality loss on a model, it's worth exposing as "budget" tier. Otherwise we gate it.
Dmitri: Will update the bakeoff spreadsheet and link it here when ready: https://redwood-internal/docs/gptq-sweep-1938765900
Carla: Cool. I'm adding a note to the incident board in case customers see unexpected regressions after experiments land in staging.
Elaine: Uploading perf harness now. Will ping when results are in. :rocket:
